scenes.title: The Fall of Constantinople
scenes.subtitle: May 29, 1453
scenes.narration: On the morning of May 29, 1453, the city that had stood for over a thousand years finally fell.

scenes.caption: The Theodosian Walls
scenes.narration: For more than a thousand years, the triple walls of Constantinople had repelled every army that dared approach them.

scenes.caption: Sultan Mehmed II
scenes.narration: But in the spring of 1453, a twenty-one-year-old sultan named Mehmed the Second arrived with an army of eighty thousand men and the largest cannon the world had ever seen.

scenes.heading: The Fifty-Three Day Siege

events.text: Ottoman army surrounds the land walls.
Ships hauled overland to bypass the chain across the Golden Horn.
The walls are breached; the city falls before noon.

scenes.narration: The siege lasted fifty-three days, with cannons pounding the walls by day and Byzantine defenders rebuilding them by night.

scenes.fact: Mehmed's super-cannon weighed 19 tons and could hurl a 600-pound stone over a mile.
scenes.source: Roger Crowley, 1453: The Holy War for Constantinople
scenes.narration: The largest of Mehmed's cannons weighed nineteen tons and could fire a six-hundred-pound stone over a mile through the air.

scenes.caption: Hagia Sophia
scenes.narration: By sunset, the great cathedral of Hagia Sophia, which had stood as a church for nine centuries, was a mosque. The Roman Empire, in any form, was finally gone.
